evidence_receipt: Section Androceras is sister to section Crinitum; Crinitum includes isantherous S. lycocarpum with independent bee/buzz-pollination evidence. Alternative Crinitum candidates were considered and SOURCE_QUALITY tie-break was frozen before BALANCE predictor extraction.

Modern Melastomateae phylogenomics places the O. chinensis/O. nepalensis lineage sister to Melastoma; Flora of China records isomorphic equal/subequal stamens; direct Hymenoptera flower-visitation evidence exists. Match is explicitly same-tribe rather than falsely congeneric.

M. australasica is source-resolved as nonheterantherous. The registered 68-shared-single-copy-CDS plastome audit ranks M. australasica closer than M. cyanea to M. korsakowii on the common-site p-distance surface. That closes the phylogenetic ranking conditional on ecological eligibility, not the closest-eligible-control gate itself. Direct species-level effective animal-pollination evidence remains OPEN for the candidate set, so the pair remains OPEN and M. cyanea is retained as an alternative.

The frozen search exhausts the sampled clade-II candidates as heteranthery-absence failures. In the next eligible clade-III grain, S. spectabilis and S. atomaria both satisfy the morphology criterion, but S. spectabilis has direct reproductive evidence of cross-pollination and major bee visitors. The SOURCE_QUALITY tie-break therefore selects S. spectabilis without using BALANCE predictors.

S. bicapsularis lies in heterantherous VIIa; the next eligible lineage is sister subclade VIIb, characterized by near-homomorphic fertile stamens. The sampled VIIb audit rejects S. bauhinioides and S. villosa on the heteranthery-absence gate and rejects S. armata by the preregistered SOURCE_QUALITY tie-break. S. covesii has direct seven-fertile-stamen morphology and observed small-bee buzz pollination, so all registered matching gates pass without using BALANCE predictor values.
